
# SOP - Hybrid Identity

Implementation Guide

Hybrid identity implementation is performed when extending identity and offload authentications from on-premises windows active directory domain controller to domain controller in Azure. Upon extending identity to Azure cloud, organizations building applications in azure can easily serve authentication requests without any VPN or connection issues.

As per requirements & implementation planning, virtual machine(s) will be deployed in prod subscription. Before proceeding with the implementation, the following details needs to thoroughly revised and ready.

Permissions:

1.       Domain account to on-premises environment.

2.       Contributor role on subscription

Notable points:

1.       Azure Vnet should not overlap with on-premises network (address spaces).

2.       Public IP or inbound public inbound ports should not be opened.

3.       Line of sight to on-premises network either using VPN tunnel or ExpressRoute to your azure network.

4.       No spot VMs will be used for DCs in Azure.

![Deploy AD DS in an Azure virtual network - Azure Architecture Center | Microsoft Learn](data:image/png;base64,)

**Configurations on on-premises DC:**

1.       Create two sites for Azure prod and Azure DR.

2.       Configure network address spaces for both sites.

## Deploy 1st Production Domain Controller:

1.       Login into Azure portal ([https://portal.azure.com](https://portal.azure.com))

2.       Subscription: Select the subscription you want to use for the VM.

3.       Resource group: Select an existing or create a new resource group.

4.       Virtual machine name: Give your VM a name (AZ-DC01)

5.       Region: Choose the first region to deploy 1st production-based DC.

6.       Availability options: Select Zone 1 (and Zone 2).

7.       Security Type: Choose Trusted Launch Virtual Machine.

8.       Image: Choose “Windows Server 2019 Datacenter”.

9.       Size: For default choice, choose Azure VM size of “Standard_D2s_v5” which will have 2 Cores and 8 GB of RAM.

10.   Username and password: This will be the local administrator account for the VM.

11.   Public inbound ports: you want this set to “none”.

12.   Licensing: If you have an existing license, you can use select the box, this can save money on each VM.

## ADDS Pre-Configuration Settings:

1.       Login into the Server that is created with admin credentials.

2.       Run ipconfig /all in cmd and verify the custom DNS settings.

3.       If clients are managing separate disk to store database, SYSVOL and logs. Follow below steps to create new data disk.

4.       Initialize and format the data disk as F:

5.       Open the Start menu and browse to Computer Management

6.       Browse to Storage > Disk Management

7.       Initialize the disk as MBR.

8.       Create a New Simple Volume and Assign the drive letter ‘F’ (you can provide a Volume label if you wish)

## AD DS Configuration:

1.       Access the Azure VM through RDP then launch server manager.  
![](data:image/png;base64,)

2.       Install AD DS server role.  
Go to role and features >>  

3.       Click Next >> Next >> on the **Server Role** Plate  
Select **Active Directory Domain Services** and add the Feature  
![](data:image/png;base64,)  
Do Next and start Installing.

4.       After Installation Restart the server.

5.       Then do the Domain join of the server to the onprem Domain.  
(Before Joining try to ping the onpremises DC through Private IP such that we have the VM in the secured Network. Go to command prompt and try command “ping <private IP of VM>)

6.       For doing the domain Join  
GO on **Local Server** and click on **Workgroup**  

7.       System Properties Dialog box will Open. In the Computer Name slide Click on **Change**.  

8.       Select Domain and write the Domain Name of the onprem.



9.       Then it will ask for credentials of the Administrator of the Onprem DC. Just fill the credentials and click OK.  



10.   And after successful connection you will see a popup like  

## Promoting the azure server to DC

1.     Now after the successful AD Join. Now promote the server to DC such that on the top right there is flag Icon which will say to promote the server to DC. CLICK On It.

2.     The page will open like this.  
Select “**Add a domain controller to an existing domain**”Fill the domain name that you have example “corp.org”.  
after that it will ask for the ADMIN CREDENTIALS of the onprem-DC fill the details and select OK.  
NOTE: Be ready with the Admin Credentials of the server from before.  
  

3.     After filling the credentials, You will receive a popup as “WELCOME to the DOMAIN”.  
  

4.     Specify the capabilities you want that server to have in the environment


and in which site you want that server to be. By default, it will show the ‘Default first site”. So, the sites you have in your Domain Controller which is running that domain(corp.org).  
Give the DSRM password for the server which will be used to restore the server. Usually, the DSRM password is set same for all the servers in the domain, as it will be easy for the org to restore the servers.  
  

5.     Select the DC from the drop-down list.  
Click Next.  



6.     Provide the path for storing the ADDS data  
 
If clients are managing separate disk to store database, SYSVOL and logs.  
Visit the ADDS prerequisites and configure the storage.  
This is the last step after this the forest and domain schema preparation is performed. Review the deployments and then INSTALL.

7.     After the installation you must restart the server and give the admin credentials of the domain.  
And then check the replication status.

## Check the replication status!

For checking replication go to PowerShell and run the command  
**repadmin /replsummary**(there is space before “/”).

If the result is like this  

then congratulations, you have successfully connected the DCs and they are replicated successfully.  
NOTE: Replication can take some time.
